data.title: Counting Knister Scores
data.statement:
Knister is a dice game played on a 5×5 scorecard. Each round, two six-sided dice are rolled and the player writes their sum (a number from 2 to 12) in an empty cell. After 25 rounds the card is full and gets scored.

The card is scored line by line. There are 12 lines: the 5 rows, the 5 columns and the 2 diagonals. Every cell belongs to several lines; the centre cell even belongs to four.

Each line scores points for the combination formed by its five numbers:

```
Combination       Definition           Points  Example
---------------------------------------------------------
Pair              Only one value         1     4 5 6 7 5
                    appears exactly
                    twice
Two pairs         Two distinct values    3     5 6 6 10 5
                    appear exactly
                    twice each
Three of a kind   One value appears      3     7 8 7 7 4
                    exactly three
                    times
Full house        Three of a kind        8     4 9 4 4 9
                    plus a pair

Four of a kind    One value appears      6     6 3 6 6 6
                    exactly four
                    times
Five of a kind    One value appears     10     8 8 8 8 8
                    exactly five
                    times
Straight          7 appears in a         8     7 10 8 6 9
  containing a 7    straight

Straight          7 does not appear     12     3 5 6 2 4
  without a 7       in a straight
```

- A straight is five consecutive numbers, in any order. Straights do not wrap around: for example, 10 11 12 2 3 is not a straight.
- <<A line scores exactly one combination>>: the one that describes all five numbers. A smaller combination formed by a subset of the five numbers does not count. For example, a full house scores 8, not 3 + 1.
- A line without any of these combinations scores 0.
- <<Points scored on the two diagonals are doubled.>>

(7 is the most likely sum of two dice, so a straight that avoids it is rarer and worth more.)

Output the total score of the scorecard.

Example

      

         

            
Input

            
5 6 9 2 7
3 10 8 10 5
4 5 11 6 10
7 9 4 8 2
12 4 5 7 6

1
